description: Standing Capability Ledger for this repository. Re-installed by the human on approving escalation D-001 (2026-09-13) after the runtime moved to .harness/knowledge/. Migrated verbatim from the prior ledger at knowledge/capabilities.json (approved 2026-09-10, corrected 2026-09-11 to withdraw the updateDebugScreenshotTest grant). Standing = per-repository toolchain that survives this goal and future runs. The runtime reads only the 'allow' arrays, verbatim.

entries.intent: Build, unit-test and lint the app so task completion can be evidenced (ENGINE.md §6.7, §6.10). The engine currently holds no build capability in this repository; without this, no task can ever be marked complete. Includes the dependency resolution Gradle performs as part of these tasks.

Verify rendered UI against the recorded reference images, so acceptance criteria about appearance, contrast and layout are provable by command output instead of being narrowed away. Host-side (layoutlib on the JVM) - no emulator, no device, no adb. Read-only with respect to the references: it compares, it never overwrites.

entries._withheld: updateDebugScreenshotTest is DELIBERATELY ABSENT from this ledger.
entries._why: It overwrites the committed reference images. An engine holding it, facing a red screenshot test, has a one-command route to making the failure disappear by re-recording wrong output as correct - the same class of act as editing an approved DoD. Granted standing on 2026-09-10, withdrawn on 2026-09-11; not re-granted here.
entries._how_to_grant: When a baseline genuinely must move - an intentional UI change, or a new state that has no reference yet - the engine raises an Escalation Request and the human adds a GOAL-SCOPED entry to .harness/run/capabilities.json (not here), which expires with the run.
entries.intent: placeholder - no capability is granted by this entry

Read files out of earlier commits and out of a prior run's Loop Branch. Bash(git show*) is already baseline, but on Windows/Git Bash MSYS rewrites 'ref:path' into 'ref;path' and the command fails for exactly the paths that matter (.harness/**, knowledge/**), with an error that reads as if the file is missing. MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 is the documented workaround, and the leading assignment means the baseline rule does not match it.
